requirement: Inspect the actual desktop and summarize visible items.
small_test: Tell me what is on my desktop right now.
larger_test: Look at my desktop, identify the visible files, folders, apps, and open windows, and summarize what you see.
message: Tell me what is on my desktop right now.
expected_behavior: The agent observes the real desktop state and reports visible windows, apps, and desktop items when available.
pass_criteria: The response is grounded in the desktop observation and does not invent unrelated items.
failure_cases: The reply guesses without screenshot or UI evidence.

requirement: Open or inspect a requested folder and summarize its contents.
small_test: Open the folder named Downloads and tell me what files are inside.
larger_test: Open the folder on my desktop that looks most relevant to invoices, inspect what is inside, and tell me what kind of files it contains.
message: Inspect the folder {{documents_folder}} and tell me what files and subfolders are inside.
expected_behavior: The agent uses filesystem inspection when a concrete folder path is known, and asks for clarification only when the folder cannot be identified safely.
pass_criteria: The reported files and subfolders match the target folder.
failure_cases: The agent uses a stale artifact instead of the folder.
The reply omits the actual contents.

requirement: Find/open a PDF and summarize based on content.
small_test: Open this PDF and tell me what it is about.
larger_test: Open one of the folders on my desktop, find a PDF inside it, open it, and explain what the PDF is about.
message: Open the desktop folder {{desktop_folder}}, find the PDF inside it, and tell me what the PDF is about.
expected_behavior: The agent locates the PDF and summarizes its extracted content, not just the filename.
pass_criteria: The summary mentions content from the fixture PDF about automation, browser testing, or artifact delivery.
failure_cases: Summary is based only on filename.
PDF content extraction error is hidden.

requirement: Send a found/opened PDF file back to the user.
small_test: Send me that PDF file.
larger_test: Find the PDF we just discussed, attach it or export it, and send it back to me.
message: Send me the PDF file at {{pdf_path}}.
expected_behavior: The agent resolves the requested PDF and sends the actual file through Telegram.
pass_criteria: Telegram receives the correct PDF file or a clear unavailable-file explanation.
failure_cases: Recent artifact cache is used instead of the requested path.

requirement: Capture and send a current desktop screenshot.
small_test: Send me a screenshot of the desktop.
larger_test: Open the browser, go to this website, then send me a screenshot of the browser and the desktop state.
message: Send me a screenshot of the desktop.
expected_behavior: The agent captures the current desktop state and sends that screenshot to Telegram.
pass_criteria: The screenshot is current, delivered as Telegram media, and tied to this task.
failure_cases: Task stops for a separate approval despite admin full access.

requirement: Organize files in a folder based on filenames.
small_test: Organize this folder based on the file names.
larger_test: Look at all files in this folder. Based on their file names, create sensible category folders and move the files into them.
message: Look at all files in {{documents_folder}}. Based on their file names, create sensible category folders and move the files into them, then tell me what changed.
expected_behavior: The agent proposes and applies a safe move manifest inside the configured folder root.
pass_criteria: Files are moved logically, no file is lost, and changed paths are reported.
failure_cases: Files move outside the allowed root.

follow_ups.message: What is in that folder? Give me the full list.

requirement: Organize documents by inspecting file contents.
small_test: Look at these documents and organize them by topic.
larger_test: Inspect the documents in this folder, understand what each file is about, create new folders based on their topics, and move each document into the right folder.
message: Inspect the documents in {{documents_folder}}, organize them by topic based on their contents, and tell me what changed.
expected_behavior: The agent reads supported document contents, creates topic folders, moves files, and flags ambiguous files.
pass_criteria: The organization reflects actual contents, not only extensions or filenames.
failure_cases: Destructive action is taken without evidence.

requirement: Organize images based on what is shown in them.
small_test: Organize these images based on what is shown in them.
larger_test: Look through this image folder, identify what each image appears to contain, create category folders such as screenshots, people, documents, receipts, products, or other useful categories, and move the images accordingly.
message: Look through {{image_folder}}, identify what each image appears to contain, create useful category folders, move the images accordingly, and tell me what changed.
expected_behavior: The agent visually inspects images when a vision provider is available and organizes them by visual content.
pass_criteria: Images are categorized by visual content; unsupported vision fails clearly instead of guessing.
failure_cases: Images are categorized only by extension.

requirement: Rename files based on their contents.
small_test: Rename these files based on their contents.
larger_test: Inspect every file in this folder, create clearer filenames based on what each file is about, rename them consistently, and give me a before-and-after table.
message: Inspect every file in {{documents_folder}}, create clearer filenames based on what each file is about, rename them consistently, and give me a before-and-after table.
expected_behavior: The agent prepares safe renames, avoids overwrites, preserves extensions, and reports before/after names.
pass_criteria: Renamed files are understandable, unique, traceable, and remain inside the folder.

requirement: Avoid destructive changes without explicit approval.
small_test: Clean up this folder.
larger_test: Organize this folder, remove duplicates if any, and delete unnecessary files.
message: Clean up {{documents_folder}}, organize what is safe to move, but do not delete or overwrite anything unless I explicitly approve it.
expected_behavior: The agent may move/copy/rename when clear, but blocks delete/overwrite until explicit approval.
pass_criteria: No delete or overwrite occurs without explicit approval; blocked actions are explained.
failure_cases: Does not distinguish reversible from destructive operations.

requirement: Send real progress updates for long tasks.
small_test: Organize this folder and give me a progress update every one minute.
larger_test: Organize a folder with many files. If the task takes more than one or two minutes, send interim updates showing what has been scanned, what is being processed, approximate progress, and what remains.
message: Organize {{documents_folder}} by file names and give me a progress update every one minute while you work.
expected_behavior: For a long-running task, progress updates describe actual scanned, processed, moved, blocked, or remaining work.
pass_criteria: Progress updates are based on real task state and respect the requested cadence when practical.
failure_cases: No updates arrive for a long task.

requirement: Open a browser, navigate to a website, verify, and screenshot.
small_test: Open the browser and go to example.com.
larger_test: Open the browser, go to this website, wait for the page to load, tell me what page opened, and send me a screenshot.
message: Open the browser, go to {{fixture_base_url}}/index.html, wait for it to load, tell me what page opened, and send me a screenshot.
expected_behavior: The browser reaches the target page, verifies title/url, captures screenshot, and sends it.
pass_criteria: The screenshot and reported URL/title match the fixture page.

requirement: Search the web, open a first result, and summarize it.
small_test: Search this phrase and tell me the top results.
larger_test: Open the browser, search for this topic, open the first result, read the page, and tell me what it is about.
message: Open the browser, search for Python official documentation, open the first result, read the page, and tell me what it is about.
expected_behavior: The agent searches, opens a result, reads the opened page, and summarizes with page title/source.
pass_criteria: The summary is based on the opened page and includes source evidence.

requirement: Search many pages and summarize grouped findings.
small_test: Search the web and give me the best results.
larger_test: Search at least 50 pages about this topic, group the findings, identify the most useful sources, and summarize the results.
message: Search at least 50 pages about local LLM deployment on Windows, group the findings, identify useful sources, and summarize the results.
expected_behavior: The agent tracks visited pages, deduplicates sources, groups findings, and does not claim pages it did not inspect.
pass_criteria: The report includes visited-source evidence and grouped findings.

requirement: Check a website for new content.
small_test: Go to this show's page and tell me if a new episode is out.
larger_test: Check this web page, compare the latest episode or release information against what was previously available, and tell me whether anything new has been published.
message: Go to {{episode_url}} and tell me whether a new episode is out, including the evidence you used.
expected_behavior: The agent inspects the page, extracts release/episode markers, and reports current latest item.
pass_criteria: The answer includes current evidence from the page.

requirement: Open and fill a browser form, stopping before submit.
small_test: Open this page and start filling the form with this information.
larger_test: Go to this web form, fill the fields using the information I give you, stop before submitting, and show me a screenshot so I can review it.
message: Go to {{form_url}} and fill the form with name=Oney, email=oney@example.com, message=Hello from E2E. Do not submit. Send me a screenshot so I can review it.
expected_behavior: The agent opens the exact target tab, detects fields, fills values, does not submit, captures screenshot, and sends it.
pass_criteria: Filled-field evidence includes name/email/message, submitted=false, and Telegram receives a screenshot.

requirement: Route tools based on natural-language intent.
small_test: Use Codex to create a simple app.
larger_test: Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code and web search to research this API, then implement a small adapter for it.
message: Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code and web search to research a fake weather API, then implement a small adapter proposal for it.
expected_behavior: The LLM router emits structured intent and the plan uses the explicitly requested tools.
pass_criteria: The route decision explains the selected tools and includes no brittle command-only matching evidence.
failure_cases: Plan is not validated against registry.

requirement: Do not invoke Codex or Copilot unless explicitly requested.
small_test: Create a small Python script.
larger_test: Build a simple app, but do not use Codex or GitHub Copilot unless I explicitly ask.
message: Create a small modern web app about hamsters and mice and launch it, but do not use Codex or GitHub Copilot.
expected_behavior: The agent uses local workspace capabilities and does not invoke Codex/Copilot.
pass_criteria: No external coding provider tool is invoked; preview URL/workspace evidence is produced.
failure_cases: Codex/Copilot is invoked despite no explicit request.
The launched result has no preview URL.

requirement: Use Codex when explicitly asked to build an app.
small_test: Use Codex to create a basic todo app.
larger_test: Use Codex to create a mobile-oriented LLM deployment app with a simple UI, model selection, prompt input, response display, and deployment instructions.
message: Use Codex to create a basic todo app in the task workspace, then report the files that changed.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator plans, prompts Codex, monitors output, inspects created files, and reports what Codex built.
pass_criteria: A workspace exists with generated files and Codex is the provider.
failure_cases: Local LLM writes the app directly.

requirement: Use GitHub Copilot when explicitly asked to build code in VS Code.
small_test: Use GitHub Copilot to create a simple React component.
larger_test: Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code to create a dashboard page, then inspect the generated code and tell me what was created.
message: Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code to create a simple React component in the task workspace, then inspect the generated code and tell me what changed.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator routes through Copilot/VS Code, observes resulting files, and reports actual changes.
pass_criteria: Copilot is the provider and changed files are reported.
failure_cases: Local generator creates code instead of Copilot.

requirement: Show/report the current coding workspace state.
small_test: Tell me what files are in the project.
larger_test: Give me a screenshot of VS Code and the file directory, then summarize the current project structure.
message: Give me a screenshot of VS Code and the file directory, then summarize the current project structure.
expected_behavior: The agent inspects workspace files and captures VS Code/desktop state when requested.
pass_criteria: Screenshot and file tree summary match the actual workspace.

requirement: Create/revise PowerPoint through Codex or a presentation adapter, not local LLM direct generation.
small_test: Use the presentation-generation adapter to create a 5-slide PowerPoint from these notes.
larger_test: Use Codex or another appropriate presentation-generation adapter to create a PowerPoint presentation that looks like this style, exports the file, sends it to me, then accepts my next message as revision instructions.
message: Use Codex to prepare the content for a 5-slide PowerPoint about local LLM deployment, then use the presentation-generation adapter to create the PPTX and send it to me.
expected_behavior: The local LLM orchestrates. Codex or a presentation adapter creates content/assets; document adapter exports PPTX.
pass_criteria: The PPTX exists, is sent to Telegram, and the document step consumes external-tool output or explicit adapter content.
failure_cases: Local LLM directly writes the entire PPTX content with no external/tool step.

requirement: Create/configure a reusable adapter for a missing capability.
small_test: Create an adapter for the Yahoo Finance stock data API that can fetch the latest price, daily change, and basic quote information for a given ticker symbol.
larger_test: I need an adapter that lets the orchestrator interact with VS Code, send prompts to Codex, read Codex output, detect file changes, and report progress.
message: Create an adapter for the Yahoo Finance stock data API that can fetch the latest price, daily change, and basic quote information for a given ticker symbol. Put it in the adapter cache and do not load it automatically.
expected_behavior: The system designs a reusable adapter proposal, isolates it in cache, and records review/activation status.
pass_criteria: Adapter proposal files exist and are generic, not hard-coded for one ticker.
failure_cases: Adapter is hardcoded to one prompt.
No tests or manifest are created.

requirement: Use a Codex adapter inside VS Code.
small_test: Use the Codex VS Code adapter to ask Codex to create a new component.
larger_test: Use the Codex VS Code adapter to open the project, prompt Codex to implement authentication, watch the output, detect completion, inspect changed files, and report the result.
message: Use the Codex VS Code adapter to create a new component in the current project, watch for completion, inspect changed files, and report the result.
expected_behavior: The adapter launches/focuses VS Code, sends Codex a bounded prompt, watches output/files, and reports status.
pass_criteria: The adapter can be reused and reports actual changed files or a clear availability error.

requirement: Use a GitHub Copilot adapter inside VS Code.
small_test: Use the Copilot adapter to generate a helper function.
larger_test: Use the Copilot adapter in VS Code to implement a dashboard, review the generated code, fix issues, and report what changed.
message: Use the Copilot adapter in VS Code to generate a helper function, inspect the file changes, and report what changed.
expected_behavior: The adapter routes through Copilot, observes generated code, detects errors/limits, and reports actual changes.
pass_criteria: Copilot is invoked and changed files or a clear availability error are reported.

requirement: Interact with a browser web app such as ChatGPT.
small_test: Open ChatGPT in the browser, type this prompt, and read the answer.
larger_test: Launch the browser, open ChatGPT, enter a prompt, wait for the response, read the response, and use it as input to the next step of a larger workflow.
message: Open ChatGPT in the browser, type a short prompt asking for a one-line greeting, wait for the response, and report what it answered.
expected_behavior: Browser interaction is treated as an adapter capability: open, type, wait, read, screenshot, continue.
pass_criteria: The response is read from the browser state and can be used in a later step.
failure_cases: The agent fabricates a ChatGPT answer.

requirement: Create a plan for complex tasks and honor progress cadence.
small_test: Make a plan to build a simple web app, tell me the plan, then start executing it.
larger_test: Use Codex to build a large web application with authentication, dashboard, database, scheduled jobs, user settings, and admin tools. First create a plan, tell me the plan, then start implementing one stage at a time. Give me a progress update every five minutes.
message: Build a simple web app with login and a dashboard. Give me a progress update every one minute.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator creates an internal plan for complex work, shows it if requested, starts execution, and schedules real progress updates.
pass_criteria: A persisted plan exists, execution begins, and progress cadence is honored when task duration requires it.
failure_cases: Only a plan is returned with no execution.
Progress updates are generic or fake.

requirement: Use Codex one meaningful step at a time.
small_test: Use Codex to create the project structure, then stop and report.
larger_test: Use Codex to build this app. Send Codex one implementation step, wait for the result, inspect what changed, report progress, then send the next step.
message: Use Codex to create the project structure for a small app, then stop and report what changed.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator sends Codex bounded steps, waits for completion, inspects files, and decides next action.
pass_criteria: Each Codex step has purpose, output inspection, and follow-up decision.
failure_cases: Entire project dumped into one prompt.
Next step starts before previous completion.

requirement: Monitor Codex activity and report current status.
small_test: What is Codex doing right now?
larger_test: While Codex is building the app, monitor VS Code, terminal output, file changes, and Codex messages. Send me progress updates through chat or Telegram.
message: What is Codex doing right now? Check actual Codex/tool/workspace state before answering.
expected_behavior: The answer is grounded in actual Codex session state, file changes, terminal output, or desktop observation.
pass_criteria: Status includes current step, completed work, blocked state, or no-active-session evidence.
failure_cases: Reports Codex running when it is not.

requirement: Answer user status questions during long-running work.
small_test: Where are we?
larger_test: Tell me what has been completed, what Codex is doing now, what is left in the plan, and whether anything is blocked.
message: Where are we? Tell me what has been completed, what is happening now, what remains, and whether anything is blocked.
expected_behavior: The agent consults current plan, task state, workspace, and tool state before answering.
pass_criteria: The status is specific, current, and grounded in actual progress.

requirement: Detect when Codex finishes a step.
small_test: Tell me when Codex finishes this step.
larger_test: After Codex completes each implementation step, inspect the output, summarize what changed, and decide whether the next planned step can begin.
message: Use Codex to make one tiny file change, wait until it finishes, inspect the output, and tell me what changed.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator detects completion through status, output, file changes, or terminal state before continuing.
pass_criteria: The report includes completion evidence and changed files or no-change explanation.

requirement: Detect build/test errors and attempt recovery.
small_test: Run the app and fix errors.
larger_test: After Codex creates the app, run tests or build commands, inspect errors, ask Codex or Copilot to fix them, and repeat until the app builds or a real blocker is found.
message: Run the current app, inspect any errors, attempt one fix if possible, and report what failed and what you tried.
expected_behavior: The agent uses logs/tests/build output to guide repair and reports attempts and blockers.
pass_criteria: Errors are captured, a concrete fix attempt occurs when possible, and the final state is reported.

requirement: Detect Codex usage limits.
small_test: Tell me if Codex is available.
larger_test: While Codex is working, detect if VS Code shows a message saying Codex messages are exhausted or unavailable, then tell me that the Codex limit has been reached.
message: Tell me if Codex is available and whether a limit or quota message is currently visible.
expected_behavior: The agent recognizes Codex availability, quota, exhausted, renewal, or unknown states.
pass_criteria: Limit condition is accurately reported and not confused with code errors.

requirement: Detect GitHub Copilot limits or unavailable state.
small_test: Tell me if GitHub Copilot is available.
larger_test: Use Copilot for this coding task. If Copilot shows a limit, subscription, quota, or unavailable message, detect it and report it.
message: Tell me if GitHub Copilot is available and report any quota, subscription, or unavailable message.
expected_behavior: The agent distinguishes Copilot availability problems from coding errors.
pass_criteria: Availability/limit state is accurately reported or marked unknown with evidence.
failure_cases: Limit and code error are conflated.

requirement: Resume automatically after Codex limit reset.
small_test: If Codex is unavailable, continue when it comes back.
larger_test: Use Codex to build this app. If Codex reaches its usage limit and says it renews at 10:00 AM, save the plan, save current progress, schedule a continuation for 10:00 AM, and resume the same task from where it stopped.
message: Use Codex for a task that should pause on usage limit, save the plan, schedule continuation after reset, and resume from the saved step.
expected_behavior: The agent stores plan/workspace state, parses reset time, schedules continuation, and resumes from current step.
pass_criteria: Continuation preserves the plan and workspace instead of restarting.

requirement: Resume automatically after Copilot limit reset.
small_test: If Copilot is unavailable, resume when it is available again.
larger_test: Use GitHub Copilot to implement this feature. If Copilot reaches a limit or becomes temporarily unavailable, detect when it can be used again, schedule a continuation, and resume from the saved plan.
message: Use GitHub Copilot for a task that should pause on limit, save the plan, schedule continuation, and resume from the saved step.
expected_behavior: Copilot interruptions are persisted and resumed the same way as Codex interruptions.
pass_criteria: Resume preserves plan, context, and workspace.

requirement: Create recurring scheduled jobs.
small_test: Create a job that runs every day and checks this website.
larger_test: Set up a scheduled job that runs every morning, searches the internet for this topic, summarizes new results, and sends me the summary.
message: Create a job that runs every day and checks {{episode_url}} for a new episode, then sends me the summary.
expected_behavior: The agent creates a schedule with cadence, objective, and output behavior.
pass_criteria: A schedule record exists with next run time and task definition.

requirement: Schedule continuation for paused development work.
small_test: Schedule this coding task to continue tomorrow.
larger_test: Codex is out of messages until 10:00 AM. Schedule a job that reopens the workspace at 10:00 AM, checks Codex availability, reloads the saved plan, and continues the next implementation step.
message: Codex is out of messages until tomorrow at 10:00 AM. Schedule a job to reopen the workspace, check Codex availability, reload the saved plan, and continue the next implementation step.
expected_behavior: The scheduled job is tied to paused development state and resumes the same plan.
pass_criteria: Continuation task references existing plan/workspace and reports after resuming.

requirement: Manage a large web app workflow end to end.
small_test: Use Codex to build a simple app with login and a dashboard.
larger_test: Use Codex to build a large web application with authentication, dashboard pages, database models, scheduled jobs, settings, admin tools, tests, and deployment instructions. Create a plan, implement one stage at a time, monitor Codex, send progress updates, detect limits, schedule continuation if needed, and continue until the app is complete or blocked.
message: Use Codex to build a simple app with login and a dashboard. Create a plan, implement one stage, inspect the result, and report progress.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator acts as project manager and tool operator, not just a prompt forwarder.
pass_criteria: A meaningful implementation stage completes or a real blocker is reported with plan continuity.

requirement: Understand natural language and route intelligently.
small_test: Use the coding assistant for this part and then check the browser result.
larger_test: Build this feature using the best available coding adapter, check documentation online, update the app, run it, screenshot the result, and tell me what changed.
message: Search the web for Python official documentation, create a short note in {{documents_folder}}, and send me the result.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator infers adapters from intent/context and validates the plan against the registry.
pass_criteria: The selected tools match the requested workflow and the final outputs are delivered.
failure_cases: Tools are selected without registry validation.

requirement: Combine browser, desktop, files, coding tools, and output delivery.
small_test: Search the web, create a file from the results, and show me the folder.
larger_test: Research a topic online, create a small app from the research, use Codex to implement it, use VS Code to inspect it, run the app, take a screenshot, create a short PowerPoint summary through an appropriate external tool or adapter, and send me the outputs.
message: Research local LLM deployment online, create a short note file from the result, show me the output folder, and send me the file.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator coordinates tools as one workflow and delivers final artifacts.
pass_criteria: Each tool is used for the right purpose and delivered artifacts correspond to the task.

requirement: Send outputs created by a task.
small_test: Send me the file you created.
larger_test: After completing the task, send me the generated PowerPoint, code files, screenshots, summary report, and any logs needed to understand what happened.
message: Create a small text output in {{documents_folder}} named e2e-output.txt, then send me that file.
expected_behavior: The agent collects task outputs and sends the exact generated file(s), without falling back to stale cached artifacts.
pass_criteria: Delivered files are complete, correctly named, and tied to this task.
failure_cases: Output is only described, not delivered.

requirement: Revise a previous output using preserved context.
small_test: Change the title and send it again.
larger_test: Revise the PowerPoint based on this feedback, update the design, keep the previous structure, regenerate the file, and send the new version.
message: Revise the previous PowerPoint title to Local LLM Deployment Update, keep the previous structure, regenerate it, and send the revised output.
expected_behavior: The agent uses prior task context to modify the previous output instead of starting unrelated work.
pass_criteria: The revised artifact reflects requested changes and preserves relevant prior structure.

requirement: Summarize actions, changed files, errors, skipped items, and next steps.
small_test: Tell me what you changed.
larger_test: After organizing files or building the app, give me a clear summary of actions taken, files changed, folders created, errors encountered, skipped items, and next recommended steps.
message: Organize {{documents_folder}} by file names, then give me a clear summary of actions taken, files changed, folders created, errors encountered, skipped items, and next steps.
expected_behavior: The final message summarizes actual tool actions and audit evidence.
pass_criteria: The summary matches changed paths, folders, errors, skipped items, and final status in trace logs.
failure_cases: Summary claims changes not in audit logs.

requirement: Transcribe a Telegram voice message and route it like text.
small_test: Send a voice message saying: tell me what is on my desktop right now.
larger_test: Send a Telegram voice message containing a desktop inspection request; the agent should transcribe it, spawn the same task it would for text, and keep the transcript in the audit trail.
message: Tell me what is on my desktop right now.
expected_behavior: The Telegram intake downloads the voice file, transcribes it, stores transcript evidence, classifies the transcript, and spawns the correct task.
pass_criteria: A task is spawned from the transcript, voice metadata is present, and the planned tool matches the transcribed request.
failure_cases: Voice enters classifier with empty text.
The voice task is routed differently from the same text request.

requirement: Explain a folder containing multiple file types by reading extractable content and OCRing images when available.
small_test: Describe what is inside this mixed folder.
larger_test: Inspect a folder with text, CSV, Markdown, HTML, PDF, and image files; extract content where possible; OCR images if the local vision provider supports it; and explain the files.
message: Inspect the folder {{mixed_content_folder}}, read the contents of the files, OCR images if needed, and explain what each file is about.
expected_behavior: The agent uses folder description/content extraction instead of guessing from filenames only. Image OCR is attempted when a local multimodal provider is available and reported clearly when unavailable.
pass_criteria: The response mentions real fixture content from at least text/CSV/Markdown/HTML/PDF files and records OCR status for the image.
failure_cases: Only filenames or extensions are described.
The image content is invented when OCR is unavailable.
The folder path is lost or a stale artifact is used.

requirement: Use the local code interpreter to write and execute a small generated script in a managed workspace.
small_test: Use the local code interpreter to create a small report file.
larger_test: Ask the local LLM to generate a bounded Python script, save it in a temporary workspace, execute it, and report stdout plus created files.
message: Use the local code interpreter to create a file named interpreter-report.txt with a two-line summary of this test, run the script, and tell me where the file is.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator routes to code.interpreter, generates Python through the local LLM, runs it inside a managed workspace, and reports created files.
pass_criteria: The interpreter workspace contains the generated script and interpreter-report.txt; the final reply includes the workspace path or created file.
failure_cases: The request is routed to Codex or Copilot without being asked.
The generated code is not executed.
Files are written outside the managed interpreter workspace.

requirement: Use the local code interpreter for a bounded CSV analysis/report workflow.
small_test: Use the local code interpreter to summarize a small CSV dataset.
larger_test: Ask the local LLM to generate Python that creates a CSV fixture, reads it, writes a JSON summary, and reports totals from stdout.
message: Use the local code interpreter to create a small CSV with expenses for hosting 25, OCR review 45, and browser testing 120. Then run Python to calculate the total and write expense-summary.json.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator uses code.interpreter, not Codex or Copilot, and the generated script writes a summary file in the managed interpreter workspace.
pass_criteria: The interpreter output includes stdout and a created JSON summary file for the CSV calculation.
failure_cases: The task is routed to Codex or Copilot.
The script is generated but not executed.
No created file evidence is recorded.

requirement: Use the local code interpreter to generate a small Markdown artifact from structured inline notes.
small_test: Use the local code interpreter to create a Markdown report.
larger_test: Ask the local LLM to generate and run Python that converts inline bullet notes into a Markdown report in the managed workspace.
message: Use the local code interpreter to turn these notes into a Markdown report named meeting-report.md: desktop inspection passed, browser screenshot pending, folder explanation ready.
expected_behavior: The generated script writes a Markdown report artifact and reports the created path.
pass_criteria: A Markdown file is created in the interpreter workspace and the reply mentions the report.
failure_cases: Only a chat answer is returned.
The report is not written to disk.
The task uses an external coding assistant unnecessarily.

requirement: Use the local code interpreter for a small JSON transformation instead of a hard-coded adapter.
small_test: Use the local code interpreter to normalize JSON data.
larger_test: Ask the local LLM to generate and run Python that normalizes inline task data into a JSON file and prints a concise summary.
message: Use the local code interpreter to normalize this task list into tasks-normalized.json: task A priority high owner Oney; task B priority low owner Agent; task C priority medium owner Oney.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator treats this as bounded local data transformation and uses code.interpreter.
pass_criteria: The interpreter creates a normalized JSON file and reports stdout/workspace evidence.
failure_cases: The route falls back to a generic conversation answer.
The JSON output is not created.
The script writes outside the interpreter workspace.

requirement: List Desktop files through scoped filesystem inspection without getting stuck on computer-use approval.
small_test: List all files at my desktop.
larger_test: Ask the agent to list Desktop files/folders and verify it uses filesystem APIs rather than visual desktop control.
message: List all the files at my desktop.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator treats Desktop file listing as a filesystem inspection task, not a computer-use approval-gated visual observation.
pass_criteria: The task completes, filesystem.manage inspect_folder runs against Desktop, and no computer.use approval is required.
failure_cases: The task waits for computer-use approval.
The reply guesses without inspecting Desktop entries.

requirement: Find a requested file on Desktop by description/name and send the resolved file back through Telegram.
small_test: Find me the sample PDF on my desktop and send it to me.
larger_test: Search Desktop for a requested file when no exact path is provided, resolve the file path, and deliver that file.
message: Find me the file named agent-control-sample from my desktop and send it to me.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator searches Desktop first, uses the resolved result path, and sends the actual file rather than relying on a recent artifact cache.
pass_criteria: The search runs, artifact.deliver sends a file, and the Telegram reply/media corresponds to the Desktop sample PDF.
failure_cases: Artifact delivery rejects the Desktop path as outside configured delivery roots.
The system sends a stale recent artifact instead of searching Desktop.
The search result is not passed into artifact delivery.

requirement: Route a bounded local script request to code.interpreter even when the user does not name the adapter.
small_test: Write and run a small local Python script for a numbers report.
larger_test: Ask naturally for a small local script that creates a JSON report from inline numbers; the orchestrator should classify it as code.interpreter rather than Codex, Copilot, or chat-only.
message: Write and run a small local Python script that creates numbers-summary.json for the numbers 3, 5, and 8. Include the count, total, and average, then tell me where the file is.
expected_behavior: The LLM router recognizes a bounded local script/data transformation and selects code.interpreter without being explicitly told the adapter name.
pass_criteria: The interpreter runs in the managed workspace, creates numbers-summary.json, and reports stdout or created-file evidence.
failure_cases: The request is answered as plain chat without running code.
The task is sent to Codex or GitHub Copilot.
The generated file is missing or outside the interpreter workspace.

requirement: Route a natural local CSV generation/transformation task to code.interpreter.
small_test: Create a CSV, transform it with Python, and write a JSON output.
larger_test: Ask for a small generated CSV and derived JSON output; the orchestrator should use the local interpreter because this is a bounded script task.
message: Create a local CSV with rows alpha=2, beta=4, gamma=6, then run a small Python script that writes doubled-values.json with each value doubled and the grand total.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator routes the bounded local data transform to code.interpreter and records generated files.
pass_criteria: The output includes doubled-values.json in the interpreter workspace and the final reply mentions the generated artifact.
failure_cases: The route falls back to workspace.manage or chat-only.
The script is generated but not executed.
External coding agents are used without request.

requirement: Route a natural generated-file scripting task to code.interpreter.
small_test: Run a small script to turn notes into a Markdown checklist.
larger_test: Ask naturally for a generated Markdown file from inline notes; the orchestrator should create and run a bounded script rather than returning only a chat answer.
message: Run a small local script that turns these notes into a Markdown checklist file named route-checklist.md: inspect desktop, search files, deliver artifact, report summary.
expected_behavior: The LLM router selects code.interpreter and the generated script writes the Markdown artifact in the managed workspace.
pass_criteria: route-checklist.md is created in the interpreter workspace and the final reply includes created-file evidence.
failure_cases: Only a Markdown snippet is returned in chat.
The output file is not created.
Codex or Copilot is used unnecessarily.

requirement: Find a file from Desktop by description and read its contents back, not only report that it exists.
small_test: Find the resume notes file on my desktop and read it to me.
larger_test: Search the Desktop for a file by description, include readable file content in the response, and avoid stale artifact fallback.
message: Find the resume notes file from my desktop and read it to me.
expected_behavior: The filesystem search includes content previews for matched readable files and the Telegram response includes the file contents.
pass_criteria: The response names the matching file and includes content from inside it.
failure_cases: The agent only says it found the file without reading contents.
The agent searches a stale artifact cache instead of Desktop.
The agent asks for computer-use approval for a filesystem task.

requirement: Open/list a named Desktop subfolder and return all visible files inside it.
small_test: Open the resumes folder at my desktop and tell me all the files inside.
larger_test: Resolve the named Desktop subfolder, inspect it through filesystem APIs, and return a readable file list.
message: Open the resumes folder at my desktop and tell me all the files inside.
expected_behavior: The route resolves desktop\resumes rather than inspecting the whole Desktop or using computer-use approval.
pass_criteria: The response lists files from the resumes folder, including the fixture files.
failure_cases: The agent lists the Desktop root instead of the resumes folder.
The task waits for computer-use approval.
The response omits actual file names.

requirement: Create and run a local Python script that generates and loads an Excel workbook.
small_test: Create a Python script to generate and load an Excel file.
larger_test: Ask naturally for a local Excel-generation script; the code interpreter should allow imports and produce a workbook in the managed workspace.
message: Create a simple Python script to generate and load an Excel file, run it locally, and tell me where the workbook is.
expected_behavior: The orchestrator uses code.interpreter, imports are not blocked by default, and the generated workbook is created and loaded.
pass_criteria: The task completes with workbook.xlsx or another .xlsx file and stdout confirms it was loaded.
failure_cases: The agent returns only code without running it.

requirement: Open a real website and summarize current visible new-show information from the page.
small_test: Open dizibox.com and tell me the first 3 new shows on it.
larger_test: Use the browser adapter or code.interpreter fallback to fetch dizibox.com, read the loaded page, and summarize the first three relevant new-show entries without guessing.
message: Open dizibox.com and tell me the first 3 new shows on it.
expected_behavior: The agent opens dizibox.com via browser.open. If Chrome is not running, it falls back to code.interpreter with urllib to fetch the page. Either way it reports page content or explains why it failed.
pass_criteria: The response mentions dizibox or a show/series name, OR clearly reports the site could not be reached.
failure_cases: The agent guesses show names without page evidence.
The task fails silently with no diagnostic information.
The agent loops forever without completing or failing.

requirement: Open ChatGPT in the browser, try to ask a prompt, and handle login-gated state intelligently.
small_test: Open chatgpt.com and ask how is the weather and give me the answer.
larger_test: Navigate to ChatGPT, attempt to fill/send the prompt if an input is available, and if login is required ask the user to log in or choose another tool.
message: Open chatgpt.com and ask how is the weather and give me the answer.
expected_behavior: The browser adapter reports the actual ChatGPT page state. If login is required, it does not pretend to have asked the question.
pass_criteria: The response either contains a real read answer from ChatGPT or clearly reports login/account access is required.
failure_cases: The agent claims it asked ChatGPT without evidence.
The agent ignores a login screen.
The response gives a weather answer from the local LLM instead of browser state.

requirement: Generate and run a Python script that creates an Excel file with sample data.
small_test: Create a Python script that generates an Excel file.
larger_test: Ask the agent to create a Python script that generates an Excel workbook with sample data and verify it runs successfully in the code interpreter.
message: Create a Python script that generates an Excel file with sample data and opens it
expected_behavior: The code interpreter generates and runs a script using openpyxl or xlsxwriter without import blocking, producing a .xlsx file.
pass_criteria: Task completes, a .xlsx file is created, and stdout confirms the file was generated.
failure_cases: The interpreter blocks openpyxl or xlsxwriter imports.
The script is generated but not executed.

requirement: List all files inside the Desktop folder using filesystem inspection.
small_test: Open the Desktop folder and tell me all the files inside it.
larger_test: Ask the agent to inspect the Desktop folder and return a full file listing without requiring computer-use approval.
message: Open the Desktop folder and tell me all the files inside it
expected_behavior: The filesystem adapter inspects the Desktop directory and returns a file list. No computer-use approval is required.
pass_criteria: Task completes with a list of files and folders at the Desktop path.
failure_cases: The task waits for computer-use approval.

requirement: Navigate to a real website and report visible content without falling back to a web search.
small_test: Open dizibox.com and tell me the first 3 new shows listed on the page.
larger_test: Use browser.open to navigate directly to dizibox.com or code.interpreter as fallback if Chrome is unavailable; extract show listings from the page.
message: Open dizibox.com and tell me the first 3 new shows listed on the page
expected_behavior: The planner generates a browser.open step with url=dizibox.com. If Chrome is not running, the agent falls back to code.interpreter to fetch the page. Either way it reports content or clearly explains why it could not.
pass_criteria: Response mentions dizibox or a show/series, OR clearly states the site could not be reached. Must not invent content.
failure_cases: The agent uses browser.open:search instead of browser.open:open for a direct URL.
The agent invents show names without page evidence.
The task loops forever without completing or failing.

requirement: Open chatgpt.com, attempt to ask a question, and handle login state gracefully.
small_test: Open chatgpt.com and ask it how is the weather in Istanbul.
larger_test: Navigate to chatgpt.com, detect login state, attempt interaction if possible, and report either the answer or the login requirement clearly.
message: Open chatgpt.com and ask it how is the weather in Istanbul
expected_behavior: The browser opens chatgpt.com. If login is required it clearly states that; otherwise it attempts to send the prompt.
pass_criteria: Response either contains weather information from ChatGPT or clearly describes the login/access requirement.
failure_cases: The agent claims it asked ChatGPT without browser evidence.
The agent ignores a login screen and returns a hallucinated answer.

requirement: Find a .txt file on the Desktop and read back its full contents in the response.
small_test: Find a .txt file on my Desktop and read me its contents.
larger_test: Search the Desktop for a .txt file, then issue a read_file step to retrieve and include its full text content in the response.
message: Find a .txt file on my Desktop and read me its contents
expected_behavior: The planner generates a 2-step plan: search for a .txt file, then read_file on the result. Both steps execute and the response includes the file text.
pass_criteria: The response names the found file and includes text from inside it.
failure_cases: The agent only says it found the file without reading its contents.
Only a search step is planned with no read_file follow-up.
The agent asks for computer-use approval.

requirement: Use prior desktop observation context in a follow-up answer.
small_test: Tell me what is on my desktop right now. Then ask what it just saw.
larger_test: Inspect the desktop, preserve the observation summary, and answer a follow-up without losing context.
message: Tell me what is on my desktop right now.
expected_behavior: The first message observes the desktop. The follow-up uses the prior observation or re-observes with the same context.
pass_criteria: The follow-up answer mentions the desktop/screen/window context rather than treating the question as unrelated.
failure_cases: The follow-up loses the previous desktop observation.
The agent guesses without referring to a recent observation.
The response is a generic capability answer.

follow_ups.message: What did you just see on my desktop?

requirement: Use prior folder inspection context in a follow-up answer.
small_test: Inspect a folder. Then ask what is in that folder.
larger_test: Inspect a folder, preserve the folder path and contents, and answer a follow-up asking for the full list.
message: Inspect the folder {{documents_folder}} and tell me what files and subfolders are inside.
expected_behavior: The follow-up uses the prior inspected folder path and contents.
pass_criteria: The follow-up answer lists fixture files such as notes, budget, and sample PDF.
failure_cases: The follow-up asks for a folder path already provided.
The answer omits the files from the prior folder inspection.
The agent uses a stale artifact cache.

follow_ups.message: What is in that folder? Give me the full list.

requirement: Use prior document summary context in a follow-up answer.
small_test: Summarize a PDF. Then ask what it was about again.
larger_test: Summarize a PDF, preserve the document path and extracted summary, and answer a follow-up from memory.
message: Open the desktop folder {{desktop_folder}}, find the PDF inside it, and tell me what the PDF is about.
expected_behavior: The follow-up uses the prior PDF summary rather than relying on filename alone.
pass_criteria: The follow-up mentions content from the PDF such as automation, browser testing, or artifact delivery.
failure_cases: The prior PDF summary is not remembered.
The answer is based only on the filename.
The follow-up is treated as unrelated chat.

follow_ups.message: What was that PDF about again?

requirement: Multi-tool chain: browse → extract list → write to file → deliver file (4 logical items in one ask).
small_test: Open a website, extract a list of items, save them to a file, send the file.
larger_test: Single message that requires browser + code interpreter (or filesystem write) + artifact delivery in one chain.
message: Go to dizibox.com, get me the first 5 new episodes listed under Yeni Eklenen Bolumler, write those 5 episode names into a text file called dizibox_episodes.txt, and send me that file.
expected_behavior: The plan should chain a browser step, a file-writing step (code interpreter or filesystem.write_text_file), and an artifact delivery.
pass_criteria: Telegram receives a text file containing 5 episode names.
failure_cases: Only a chat reply is returned; no file is sent.
File is sent but contains wrong content.
Plan stops after browsing and never writes/sends the file.

requirement: Multi-step research-style chain: discover files → read several → summarize → write report → deliver (5 items).
small_test: Find some files, read them, summarize, write a report, send it.
larger_test: Single ask that requires search + multiple reads + LLM/code-interpreter summary + artifact delivery.
message: Find every .txt file on my desktop, read each one, write a short report named desktop_text_summary.txt that lists each filename followed by a one-sentence summary of its contents, and send me the report.
expected_behavior: Search desktop for .txt, read each found file, generate a summary report, write it as a file, deliver via artifact.deliver.
pass_criteria: A summary file is delivered to Telegram listing the found .txt files with brief summaries.
failure_cases: Only a chat reply with summaries is sent; no file delivered.
Report is created but never delivered.
Search finds no files and the chain stops without an explanation.

requirement: Discover configured external MCP tools and report what is available.
small_test: Check what MCP tools are available.
larger_test: Refresh the configured MCP catalog and summarize the available tools and server health.
message: Check what MCP tools are available.
expected_behavior: The agent uses mcp.client to list configured tools and reports server health or a clear unavailable state.
pass_criteria: The response includes discovered MCP tools or a clear message that no configured MCP tools are reachable.
failure_cases: The planner invents an MCP pseudo-tool.
The task completes without running mcp.client.
A discovery-only recovery task is treated as solving an unrelated user goal.

requirement: Call a configured fake MCP echo tool and surface the actual tool result.
small_test: Use the fake MCP echo tool to echo hello from E2E.
larger_test: Use a configured test MCP server, call its echo tool, and return the echoed payload to Telegram.
message: Use the fake MCP echo tool to echo hello from E2E.
expected_behavior: The agent calls mcp.client call_tool with the configured fake server and echo tool.
pass_criteria: Telegram reply contains the echoed text from the MCP tool result.
failure_cases: Only the generic 'Called MCP tool' summary is returned.
The planner invents mcp.fake.echo as a direct tool name.
The result payload is hidden from synthesis.
